subject: Post-call recap — capacity growth signal & recommended contract path
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina@brightpath.ai>, Evan Cho <evan.cho@brightpath.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-08T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap — capacity growth signal & recommended contract path

Hi Lina / Evan —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our 45-minute call and proposed next steps so everyone has the same view. I’ve attached a Q3 usage export and our first-pass Dedicated proposal for your review.

Key signals / pain points you called out
- Bursty RAG traffic: large spikes during business hours causing queued requests and p99 latency jumps (we saw p99 ~420–520ms in the export).
- Embedding volume: nightly batch jobs and real-time embeddings are driving unpredictable token spend.
- Strict SLA + audit requirements from your platform team — need private audit logs and long retention for traceability.

Goals we discussed
- Reduce p99 inference latency from current ~500ms down to <150ms for the RAG endpoint.
- Move predictable steady-state workload to a reserved capacity model to flatten cost and exposure.
- Onboard the summarization pipeline (new workload) by early Jan so it can be included in capacity planning.

Recommended immediate path (proposed owner / ETA)
1) Technical workshop (Ben SE) — deep dive on caching, batching, and serving profile to validate Dedicated sizing (owner: Ben Carter; target week of 11/15).
2) Legal/procurement touchpoint (Olga) — share Dedicated proposal + standard SOW and get procurement questions prioritized (owner: Olga; target ask: procurement questions by 11/22).
3) Pilot configuration (CS/Marissa) — 2-week burst pilot against a 4-GPU dedicated pool with KV prefix caching to measure p99 under load (owner: Marissa Cole; proposed window: 12/01–12/14).
4) Decision milestone — aim for a signed reserved capacity agreement by 12/10 to hit Jan rollout targets.

Attachments included: usage_report_q3.csv, redwood-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf.

Open questions for you
- For the summarization workload, do you expect realtime SLA (<200ms) or is batched (500–800ms) acceptable initially?
- Any constraints from procurement on contract term length or PO timing we should be aware of?

Next step I’ll take today: schedule the technical workshop with Ben (copied) and send the Dedicated proposal to procurement as discussed. Please reply here with preferred times for the week of 11/15.

Thanks —
Olga

Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai
[Attachment: usage_report_q3.csv (4KB CSV)]
[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf (1.2MB PDF)]

From: Lina Gomez <lina@brightpath.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Cho <evan.cho@brightpath.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-08T16:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — capacity growth signal & recommended contract path

Thanks, Olga — this is very clear and helpful. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Burst capacity: when you say "4-GPU dedicated pool" for the pilot, is there a recommended burst headroom for peak days (we saw ~3x baseline at peak)? If so, what’s the incremental cost for 1–2 days of burst per month?

2) Security/audit: our compliance team requires proof of tamper-evident logs and an export pathway. Can Marissa or Ben include a short note on retention/exports in the workshop agenda?

We can do the week of 11/15 — mornings PT work best for us (11/16 or 11/18 preferred). Evan and I will pull procurement constraints together and share by 11/18.

—Lina
Lina Gomez
Head of ML Platform, BrightPath AI
lina@brightpath.ai

On 2026-11-08T15:05:00-08:00 Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the time today...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: olga@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-08T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — technical notes & workshop agenda

Quick internal follow-up after reading the export:
- Pilot sizing: recommend starting with a 4x A100 equivalent pool with 2x burstable slots. That configuration should handle the 3x spikes Lina mentioned while keeping steady-state cost predictable.
- Optimizations to validate in workshop: prefix KV caching for conversation RAG, per-route batching limits (max 8) to protect tail latency, and a quantized embedding path for nightly bulk embeddings.
- Security note: we can propose audit log export to S3 with immutable retention (we have a recommended retention template) — Marissa can own verifying this with BrightPath.

I attached a short workshop agenda and a checklist for what we should ask BrightPath to bring (sample prompts, peak QPS traces, sample documents).

Ideas to include in the proposal update: estimated delta to per-token pricing for Dedicated vs hosted at their observed QPS (two scenarios: steady-state and peak). I’ll draft numbers once we confirm expected peak days/month.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: technical_workshop_agenda.docx (35KB DOCX)]

Perfect — thanks Lina and Ben. I’ll schedule the workshop for 11/16 at 10am PT and send a calendar invite with the agenda.

Action items recap (short):
- Olga: send updated proposal + HubSpot deal link to procurement (today).
- Ben: draft cost-delta scenarios for steady vs peak by 11/12.
- Marissa: prepare audit/retention notes for the workshop.
- Lina/Evan: procurement constraints and preferred term by 11/18.

Goal: decision milestone targeted for 12/10 so BrightPath can onboard the summarization workload in early January.

Thanks — look forward to the workshop.
Olga
